answer: The pigment detector writes to vertex, and lotus shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 128 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 233 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
